knowledge_base: LIFELINE Finding Money UK financial support knowledge base. Verified against permitted GOV.UK, Ofgem, Citizens Advice and Turn2us sources on 2026-11-07. Local schemes, supplier funds and charitable grants change frequently; users should confirm current rules with the administering body.

support_options.name: Universal Credit
support_options.description: Monthly living-cost payment for people out of work, on a low income or unable to work.
support_options.who_can_apply: People meeting age, residence and means rules.
eligibility_criteria: Usually 18 or over (some 16–17 year olds qualify); normally under State Pension age; must live in the UK; savings and investments must be £16,000 or less.
support_options.additional_notes: Household and partner circumstances affect entitlement.
support_options.income_threshold: No single cut-off; payment reduces as earnings rise.

support_options.name: Benefits entitlement check
support_options.description: Calculator links to help people estimate benefits and support; not an award or application.
eligibility_criteria: Results depend on income, savings, rent, household, age, disability and caring circumstances.
support_options.geographic_availability: UK-wide; check the relevant nation and council
support_options.application_method: Use GOV.UK calculator links or Turn2us Benefits Calculator.
support_options.additional_notes: Use results as a starting point and apply to the administering body.

support_options.name: Warm Home Discount
support_options.description: One-off electricity-bill discount credited by the energy supplier, not paid as cash.
eligibility_criteria: England and Wales automatic Core Group: billpayer/partner receives a qualifying benefit on the qualifying date; Scotland has Core and Broader Groups; supplier must participate.
support_options.geographic_availability: England, Wales and Scotland; not Northern Ireland
support_options.application_method: Usually automatic; some Scottish, park-home or supplier cases require contact/application.
support_options.additional_notes: Check the participating-supplier list and current qualifying date.
support_options.deadline: For 2026–27, letters say people needing to call must do so before 26 February 2027.

support_options.name: Energy supplier hardship support
support_options.description: Suppliers may offer payment plans, payment breaks or reductions and hardship funds for customers struggling with energy bills or debt.
support_options.who_can_apply: Domestic energy customers in financial difficulty.
eligibility_criteria: Supplier sets its own eligibility, evidence and award rules.
support_options.additional_notes: No common threshold or standard amount is stated.
documents_required: Income, expenditure and debt information if requested

support_options.name: Priority Services Register
support_options.description: Free extra help from energy companies and networks for people who may be vulnerable or need support managing energy supply.
support_options.who_can_apply: People needing extra support with electricity or gas.
eligibility_criteria: Eligibility is based on support needs; examples include disability, health, age and communication needs.
support_options.geographic_availability: UK-wide via the relevant electricity network
support_options.application_method: Apply to the electricity network; one electricity-network application covers the relevant suppliers.
support_options.additional_notes: Can apply even without an energy supplier, for example in a park home.

support_options.name: Free school meals
support_options.description: Free school meals for eligible children; infant free school meals are also available in England.
support_options.who_can_apply: Parents/carers of children at an eligible school.
eligibility_criteria: England Universal Credit route: household income £7,400 a year or less after tax and excluding benefits; other qualifying benefits and nation rules apply.
support_options.geographic_availability: Nation-specific; GOV.UK application route is for England
support_options.application_method: Apply through the local authority or school.
support_options.additional_notes: Check the relevant nation and council.
support_options.income_threshold: England UC route: £7,400 a year or less after tax, excluding benefits.

support_options.name: Free Childcare for Working Parents
support_options.description: Funded childcare for eligible working parents, delivered through an online childcare account and eligibility code.
support_options.who_can_apply: Working parents or those about to start work, including partners.
eligibility_criteria: Parent and partner must be working/about to start; minimum earnings rules apply; adjusted net income generally under £100,000 per parent; child-age rules apply.
support_options.geographic_availability: England; other UK nations have different arrangements
support_options.application_method: Set up a childcare account and apply online; give the 11-digit code to the provider.
support_options.additional_notes: The page states applications for 30 hours can be made from when the child is 23 weeks old; funded-period deadlines apply.
support_options.income_threshold: Adjusted net income generally under £100,000 per parent.

support_options.name: Personal Independence Payment
support_options.description: Tax-free help with extra living costs caused by a long-term physical or mental health condition or disability.
support_options.who_can_apply: People aged 16 or over meeting disability and residence rules.
eligibility_criteria: Usually 16 or over and under State Pension age when claiming; difficulty with daily living or mobility; condition expected to last at least 12 months; residence rules apply.
support_options.geographic_availability: England and Wales; Scotland uses Adult Disability Payment; Northern Ireland has separate administration
support_options.application_method: Start a claim by phone or textphone, then complete the process and assessment if required.
support_options.additional_notes: Award depends on how the condition affects activities, not diagnosis alone.
support_options.support_value: Daily living £76.70 or £114.60 weekly; mobility £30.30 or £80 weekly.
documents_required: Description of condition and functional impact

support_options.name: Disability Living Allowance for children
support_options.description: Support for extra care or mobility costs for a disabled child; adults cannot make a new DLA claim in England or Wales.
support_options.who_can_apply: Parent or person responsible for a disabled child under 16.
eligibility_criteria: Child under 16; care or mobility needs meet the relevant tests; residence and presence rules apply.
support_options.geographic_availability: England and Wales for new child claims; Scotland uses Child Disability Payment
support_options.application_method: Complete the child DLA claim form and send it to DWP.

support_options.name: Attendance Allowance
support_options.description: Help with personal-support costs where disability or health condition is severe enough that help looking after oneself is needed.
support_options.who_can_apply: People over State Pension age with qualifying care needs.
eligibility_criteria: Physical or mental disability/health condition; needs personal support; mobility needs alone do not qualify; no carer is required.
support_options.geographic_availability: England and Wales; Scotland uses Pension Age Disability Payment
support_options.application_method: Apply using the GOV.UK claim route.
support_options.additional_notes: May increase Pension Credit, Housing Benefit or Council Tax Reduction.

support_options.name: Carer’s Allowance
support_options.description: Payment for someone providing substantial unpaid care for a person receiving a qualifying disability benefit.
support_options.who_can_apply: People caring for someone at least 35 hours weekly.
eligibility_criteria: Care at least 35 hours a week; cared-for person receives a qualifying benefit; earnings and other benefit rules apply.
support_options.geographic_availability: England, Wales and Northern Ireland; Scotland has additional arrangements
support_options.application_method: Apply online or by post through GOV.UK.
support_options.additional_notes: May affect the cared-for person’s benefits.
support_options.income_threshold: Earnings limit applies; check current eligibility page.

support_options.name: Access to Work
support_options.description: Practical or financial help to start or stay in work where disability or health condition affects work.
support_options.who_can_apply: People with a disability or health condition who work or are about to work.
eligibility_criteria: Condition must affect work; support must relate to work, interviews or mental-health needs; award depends on circumstances.
support_options.geographic_availability: Great Britain; separate arrangements may apply in Northern Ireland

support_options.name: Disabled Facilities Grant
support_options.description: Grant to adapt a home so a disabled person can live more independently and safely.
support_options.who_can_apply: Disabled people or representatives applying through the local authority.
eligibility_criteria: Local authority must assess works as necessary and appropriate; property reasonableness applies; means test may apply to adults.
support_options.geographic_availability: England and Wales via local authorities
support_options.application_method: Apply to the local council housing or social-services department.
support_options.additional_notes: Amount and contribution depend on the work and circumstances.

support_options.name: Council Tax Reduction
support_options.description: Reduction in Council Tax for people on low income or claiming benefits.
support_options.who_can_apply: Council Tax liable homeowners or renters meeting local rules.
eligibility_criteria: Council considers income including savings, pensions and partner income, children and other adults; each council runs its own scheme.
support_options.geographic_availability: Local authority schemes in Great Britain; Northern Ireland has a separate rates scheme
support_options.application_method: Apply to the local council using the postcode finder.
support_options.income_threshold: No UK-wide threshold; council scheme applies.
support_options.support_value: Bill may be reduced by up to 100%

support_options.name: Council Tax single-person discount
support_options.description: 25% Council Tax discount where only one counted adult lives in a property.
support_options.who_can_apply: A liable adult meeting the single-person rules.
eligibility_criteria: Only one counted adult normally lives in the property; some residents are disregarded when counting adults.

support_options.name: Council Tax disabled band reduction
support_options.description: Council Tax relief for qualifying disabled adaptations or severe mental impairment circumstances.
support_options.who_can_apply: Households meeting disabled-band or severe-mental-impairment conditions.
eligibility_criteria: Disabled Band Reduction may apply where an extra room, bathroom, kitchen or indoor wheelchair space is needed because of disability; severe mental impairment rules require relevant certification/conditions.
support_options.application_method: Apply to the local council; medical certification may be required.

support_options.name: Local welfare and crisis assistance
support_options.description: Local schemes may provide emergency help with food, essential items, heating or housing costs.
support_options.who_can_apply: People facing an immediate crisis or difficulty paying essentials.
eligibility_criteria: Rules, budgets and awards are local; benefits are not necessarily required.
support_options.geographic_availability: Local-authority specific; England councils use Crisis and Resilience Fund arrangements, while devolved nations have their own schemes
support_options.application_method: Ask the local council or use Turn2us Grants Search with a postcode.
support_options.availability_status: Currently available but local budgets vary
support_options.additional_notes: Turn2us identifies Scottish Welfare Fund, Welsh Discretionary Assistance Fund and Northern Ireland local support routes.
documents_required: Evidence of crisis and essential need

support_options.name: Scottish Welfare Fund crisis grant
support_options.description: Discretionary grant for an emergency or disaster when essential costs cannot be afforded; it does not have to be repaid.
support_options.who_can_apply: People living in Scotland facing an emergency or disaster.
eligibility_criteria: Cannot afford essential costs; grants are discretionary and depend on local budget; some income/capital or hardship-payment exclusions apply.
support_options.application_method: Apply to the local council; Citizens Advice can help.

support_options.name: Turn2us charitable grants search
support_options.description: Matches people to charitable grants that may help with costs and normally do not need repayment.
support_options.who_can_apply: Anyone can search; individual charities set eligibility.
eligibility_criteria: Eligibility may depend on health, age, occupation, family background or financial need; many grants are circumstance-specific.
support_options.application_method: Complete the anonymous online search, then apply to the matched charity.
documents_required: Varies by charity; commonly identity, income and supporting evidence
